% Pattern: head/case. In a proof, a number in parentheses in bold at the
% start of a line, as \textbf{(1.1)}, heads a case of the proof, and the
% number keeps its parentheses. Seen in the gold pilot (set X).
% want theorem-1 statement/theorem 1
% want proof-1 proof - proves=theorem-1
% want head-1 other/case (1)
% want head-2 other/case (1.1)
% want head-3 other/case (2)
\documentclass{article}
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}
\begin{document}
\begin{theorem}
Every bounded set is small.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
We split the argument by the size of the set.

\textbf{(1)}, If the set is empty, there is nothing to show.

{\bf (1.1)} If it has one point, the point is its own bound.

\textbf{(2)}, Otherwise we take the largest point.
\end{proof}
\end{document}
